descriptionChirho: A physical piece of furniture for sleeping or reclining, including all pronominal and prepositional inflections referring to the concrete object.
The room or private quarters where one sleeps, used metonymically for the place of rest rather than the furniture itself.
Euphemistic use for the act of sexual relations, typically in the construct plural mishkeve (lyings of) or with the preposition denoting cohabitation.
The abstract act of reclining, sleeping, or resting, referring to the activity rather than the place or furniture.
